questions.stem:
A particle $P$ of mass 1.5 kg moves under the action of a single force $\mathbf{F}$ newtons.
At time $t$ seconds, $t \geqslant 0$, $P$ has velocity $\mathbf{v}\,\mathrm{m\,s}^{-1}$, where
$\mathbf{v} = (5t^2-t^3)\mathbf{i}+(2t^3-8t)\mathbf{j}$

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) M1: Differentiate – at least 3 powers going down by 1: use $\mathbf{a}=\frac{d\mathbf{v}}{dt}$. A1: $\mathbf{a}=(10t-3t^2)\mathbf{i}+(6t^2-8)\mathbf{j}$. DM1: Substitute $t=2$ and use $\mathbf{F}=m\mathbf{a}$, dependent on preceding M1: $\mathbf{F}=1.5\times((20-12)\mathbf{i}+(24-8)\mathbf{j})$. A1: $\mathbf{F}=12\mathbf{i}+24\mathbf{j}$ (ignore magnitude of $\mathbf{F}$ if found).
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Allow column vectors throughout

parts.label: b
parts.text:
At time $t=0$, $P$ is at the origin $O$.
(b) Find the position vector of $P$ relative to $O$ at the instant when $P$ is moving in the direction of the vector $\mathbf{j}$
(4)
parts.mark_scheme: (b) B1: $5t^2-t^3=0 \Rightarrow t=5$ (not moving when $t=0$ so no need to mention $t=0$). M1: Use of $\mathbf{r}=\int \mathbf{v}\,dt$ (integrate to find $\mathbf{r}$ – at least 3 powers going up by 1). A1: $\mathbf{r}=\left(\frac{5}{3}t^3-\frac{1}{4}t^4\right)\mathbf{i}+\left(\frac{1}{2}t^4-4t^2\right)\mathbf{j}$ (condone if no constant of integration seen, since $t=0, \mathbf{r}=\mathbf{0}$). A1: Final answer $\mathbf{r}=\left(\frac{625}{12}\right)\mathbf{i}+\left(\frac{425}{2}\right)\mathbf{j}$ or better $\left(52.08\dot{3}\mathbf{i}+212.5\mathbf{j}\right)$.

questions.stem: A uniform rod, of length $8a$ and mass $M$, has one end freely hinged to a fixed point $A$ on a vertical wall. One end of a light inextensible string is attached to the rod at the point $B$, where $AB=5a$. The other end of the string is attached to the wall at the point $C$, where $AC=5a$ and $C$ is vertically above $A$. The rod rests in equilibrium in a vertical plane perpendicular to the wall with angle $BAC=70^\circ$, as shown in Figure 3.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find, in terms of $M$ and $g$, the tension in the string.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme: (a) M1: Moments about $A$: need all terms and dimensionally correct. Condone sign errors, incorrect angles and sin/cos confusion. Or complete method to form equation in $T$ (and $M$). A1: $5a\times T\sin55^\circ = 4a\cos20^\circ\times Mg$ (correct unsimplified equation in $T$ and $M$). A1: $T=\frac{4\cos20^\circ}{5\sin55^\circ}Mg\,(=0.918Mg)$ or equivalent (exact or 0.92$Mg$ or better).

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The magnitude of the force acting on the rod at $A$ is $\lambda Mg$, where $\lambda$ is a constant.
(b) Find, to 2 significant figures, the value of $\lambda$.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) M1: Resolve vertically. Need all terms. Condone sign errors, incorrect angle and sin/cos confusion. A1: $Mg=V+T\cos55^\circ$ ($V=0.4736..Mg$). M1: Resolve horizontally. Condone consistent sin/cos confusion. A1: $H=T\sin55^\circ$ ($H=0.7517..Mg$). M1: Resultant $\lambda=\sqrt{(0.4736..)^2+(0.7517..)^2}$ (substitute for $T$ and use Pythagoras). A1: $=0.89$ (the Q asks for 2sf). Alternative for (b): Moments about $B$: $Mga\cos20^\circ+5aH\cos70^\circ=5aV\cos20^\circ$ (M1 dimensionally correct, need all terms, condone sign errors and sin/cos confusion; A1 correct unsimplified equation); Moments about $C$: $5aH=4aMg\cos20^\circ$ (M1 dimensionally correct; A1 correct unsimplified equation); M1: Resultant $\lambda=\sqrt{(0.4736..)^2+(0.7517..)^2}$ using Pythagoras; A1: $=0.89$ (M1A1M1A1 for 2 independent equations, M1A1 to solve for $\lambda$).
Official notes (completeness pass):
- A1: $Mg=V+T\cos55^\circ$ Correct unsimplified equation in $T$ or their $T$
- A1: $H=T\sin55^\circ$ Correct unsimplified equation in $T$ or their $T$

questions.stem:
[In this question, the unit vectors $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$ are in a vertical plane, $\mathbf{i}$ being horizontal and $\mathbf{j}$ being vertically upwards.]
A small ball is projected with velocity $(6\mathbf{i}+12\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{m\,s}^{-1}$ from a fixed point $A$ on horizontal ground. The ball hits the ground at the point $B$, as shown in Figure 5. The motion of the ball is modelled as a particle moving freely under gravity.

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme: (a) M1: $-12=12-gt$ (use suvat to find time taken). A1: $t=\frac{24}{g}\,(=2.45)$. M1: $AB=6t$ (horizontal distance). A1: $=14.7\,(15)\,(\mathrm{m})$ (3sf or 2sf; not $\frac{720}{49}$ which follows use of 9.8; not $\frac{144}{g}$, do not accept $g$ in the denominator).

parts.label: b
parts.text:
When the height of the ball above the ground is more than $h$ metres, the speed of the ball is less than $10\,\mathrm{m\,s}^{-1}$
(b) Find the smallest possible value of $h$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme: (b) B1: Vertical component of velocity $=(\pm)8$. M1: $v^2=u^2+2as$ (complete method using suvat to find $h$). A1: $\Rightarrow 8^2=12^2-2gh$ (correct unsimplified equation). A1: $h=4.08\,(4.1)$ (3sf or 2sf; not $\frac{200}{49}$ which follows use of 9.8; not $\frac{40}{g}$, do not accept $g$ in the denominator). Alternative using $\mathbf{v}=\binom{6}{12}-\binom{0}{g}t \Rightarrow 12-gt=(\pm)8$ (B1 correct expression for critical value(s) of $t$), $h=12t-\frac{1}{2}gt^2$ (M1 complete method using suvat to find $h$), $=\frac{48}{g}-\frac{8}{g}$ or $\frac{240}{g}-\frac{200}{g}$ (A1 correct unsimplified equation), $h=4.08\,(4.1)$ (A1, 3sf or 2sf). Alternative using conservation of energy: $mgh+\frac{1}{2}m\times10^2=\frac{1}{2}m(12^2+6^2)$ (M1 need all terms and dimensionally correct; A(B)1 unsimplified equation with at most one error; A1 correct unsimplified equation), $h=4.08\,(4.1)$ (A1, 3sf or 2sf).

parts.label: c
parts.text:
When the ball is at the point $C$ on its path, the direction of motion of the ball is perpendicular to the direction of motion of the ball at the instant before it hits the ground at $B$.
(c) Find, in terms of $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$, the velocity of the ball when it is at $C$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) M1: $\binom{6}{-12}\cdot\binom{6}{v}=0$ (complete method to find vertical component at $C$). A1: $\Rightarrow v=3$. A1: $\mathbf{v}=6\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}\,(\mathrm{m\,s}^{-1})$ (must be a vector in terms of $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$). Note: If see $\binom{6}{12}\cdot\binom{6}{v}=0$ leading to $\mathbf{v}=6\mathbf{i}-3\mathbf{j}$ mark as a misread: M1A0A0.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Accept working in column vectors throughout apart from the final A1
